data.source_text_main_point: Police raids and voluntary closures are shutting down European file-sharing link sites, challenging the legal assumption that merely hosting torrent links is harmless.

statements.key_statement: European police raids and voluntary closures prove that hosting torrent links is not legally harmless.
statements.long_statement: Across France, the Netherlands, Finland, and Slovenia, law enforcement raids and voluntary operator decisions have recently forced major European file-sharing link sites offline. These actions collectively undermine the prevailing legal belief that simply hosting torrent links constitutes a harmless activity, proving that such hosting can be treated as a copyright violation.

statements.key_statement: SuprNova.org's voluntary closure despite its Slovenian location proves that geographic location no longer guarantees immunity from copyright enforcement.
statements.long_statement: The voluntary shutdown of SuprNova.org, a major international BitTorrent link site, is unexpected because its physical location in Slovenia was widely assumed to provide immunity from enforcement actions by American-based copyright organizations. Despite this perceived geographic protection, the site's owner chose to remove all torrent links following news of arrests and legal warnings, signaling that the site's jurisdiction no longer guarantees safety from global copyright enforcement efforts.

statements.key_statement: The SuprNova.org operator voluntarily closed the site's link section in response to peer arrests and legal warnings.
statements.long_statement: Following reports of arrests targeting administrators of prominent peer-to-peer sites and receiving formal legal warnings, the operator of SuprNova.org determined that continuing to host torrent links was no longer viable. Consequently, the decision was made to voluntarily shut down the site's link distribution section, a move driven by the realization that the legal risks had escalated beyond the point of safe operation for the service.

statements.key_statement: FinReactor, a Finnish file-sharing website, closed down. The MPAA says it is responsible for this shutdown.
statements.long_statement: The Motion Picture Association of America asserts that it is responsible for the voluntary closure of the Finnish file-sharing site FinReactor, a claim that contradicts official denials from Finnish copyright authorities who state no contact was made with them. This position implies that the U.S. industry group believes its pressure tactics were the decisive factor in shutting down the site, despite the operators' own decision to close it following legal warnings.

statements.key_statement: BitTorrent is a 2002 peer-to-peer tool that speeds up file distribution by swapping data chunks between users.
statements.long_statement: BitTorrent, a peer-to-peer file distribution tool created by programmer Bram Cohen and introduced in 2002, functions by allowing users to swap portions of files with one another rather than relying on a single centralized server, thereby enabling faster downloads for large numbers of users compared to earlier systems.
